note: Owner briefing (T66, session arena/75efdf57-zone2, 2026-11-19). Nothing on this page is applied: every suggestion is 'Proposed - awaiting owner decision', and every open question carries what is known (with a source), what is missing and how to find out. Source ids resolve against shop/data/catalog.json 'sources'.

summary.t: The front page now leads with the five products instead of the verification process. A new shop section adds one page per product, two category pages (air fryers, meat thermometers) and six question-shaped buying guides. Every dashboard from earlier sessions is still published, reachable from one 'Behind the scenes' menu and the footer.

summary.h: The five links still resolve to the same products
summary.t: All five supplied link.amazon codes were opened again on 2026-11-19 and landed on the same five listings recorded earlier: Chefman 6 Qt dual basket (B0CDY277D3), Emeril 26 QT French door oven (B09B7SB46R), Chefman 8 Qt (B08DKYBTPH), ThermoMaven instant-read (B0DHZTCNR5), CHEF iQ Sense (B0DZFD6R9Z). None of the resolved URLs carries an Associates tag.

Every 'Check today's price' button links to the observed listing with tag shopnow047c-20, is marked rel="sponsored nofollow" and is labelled '(paid link)'. Citation links to official pages are never tagged.

summary.h: The one decision that blocks everything else
summary.t: Nobody has confirmed that the five observed listings are the products you meant. The site promotes the observed destinations and says so; the intent fields stay blank until you confirm them (questions OQ-01 and OQ-02).

summary.h: The build was quietly broken - it is running again
summary.t: From PR #158 until 19 November the deploy workflow file contained unresolved merge-conflict markers. GitHub rejected it, so every check failed with zero jobs while the local replay script kept reporting 'all green'; the site kept updating through GitHub's branch-based Pages build, unchecked. Two sessions repaired the file the same day and both added a guard to the replay script; post-merge runs on main succeed again (flags F-44, F-46).

summary.h: No traffic or sales data exists yet
summary.t: Nothing has been measured, so no page on this site states a visitor, click, conversion or revenue figure. The click counter counts locally and transmits nothing until an endpoint exists (suggestion SG-S04).

suggestions.title: Take the audit pages out of search results
suggestions.why: Most published pages on this domain are dashboards and registers; only a small share are written for buyers. Search engines and visitors can land on a register instead of a guide.

options.label: A
options.text: Add a noindex robots meta tag to every dashboard page and remove them from sitemap.xml; keep them published and linked from the footer.
options.tradeoff: Audit pages stop appearing in search, which is the point

options.label: B
options.text: Move the whole audit trail to its own repository and site (as Zone3 already is) and link to it.
options.cost: Larger migration; every generator's paths change
options.tradeoff: Cleanest separation, most work

options.label: C
options.text: Leave as is.
options.tradeoff: Search engines keep indexing registers

suggestions.title: Confirm each product inside Associates Central and test one link before scaling
suggestions.why: The brief asks for one validated Special Link per product, with the click reported, before anything scales. Without it every button may be pointing at the wrong product or earning nothing.

options.label: A
options.text: For each of the five products: open the listing while signed in, generate the Special Link with the official link tool, click it once, and confirm the click appears in the report. Then send the five confirmed ASINs back so the intent fields can be filled.
options.cost: About an hour of your time in Associates Central
options.tradeoff: Needs your login; cannot be done by an agent

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the current dp/ASIN?tag= links to the observed listings and wait for the first report.
options.tradeoff: If an observed listing is not the intended product, that is discovered late

suggestions.title: Verify the site in Google Search Console and submit the sitemap
suggestions.why: It is the only way to learn which questions people actually search before writing the next guide. The sitemap already lists every page.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify with an HTML-file or meta-tag method (both work on GitHub Pages) and submit sitemap.xml.
options.tradeoff: Query data takes time to accumulate after indexing

options.label: B
options.text: Use a custom domain first, then verify the domain property.
options.tradeoff: Better long-term brand; delays measurement

suggestions.title: Give the click counter somewhere to report to
suggestions.why: The privacy-preserving counter (page views, product-link clicks, disclosure views) works but keeps counts in the visitor's browser, because GitHub Pages cannot receive data. Orders and earnings (the other two defined events) can only come from Associates reports.

options.label: A
options.text: A small first-party endpoint on a serverless platform that accepts the existing event shape (page, link label, day - no IP, no cookie).
options.cost: A hosting account and a short script
options.tradeoff: One more service to keep running

options.label: B
options.text: Self-host an open-source, cookieless analytics tool on a small server.
options.tradeoff: Full dashboards; more maintenance

options.label: C
options.text: Rely only on Search Console and the Associates click report for now.
options.tradeoff: No on-page view of which guide sends clicks

suggestions.title: Set a publishing cadence of one question-shaped guide a week
suggestions.why: Six guides exist. New guides should answer one buyer question each, link to the products they discuss, and be added to the sitemap and feed - then the next topic is chosen from measured queries, not instinct.

options.label: A
options.text: Weekly for eight weeks, alternating air-fryer and thermometer questions; review Search Console queries at week four and re-plan.
options.tradeoff: Fast learning; needs steady effort

options.label: B
options.text: Every two weeks.
options.tradeoff: Slower signal

options.label: C
options.text: Pause new guides until Search Console data exists.
options.tradeoff: Nothing new for search engines to find

suggestions.title: Publish a seasonal turkey-temperature guide before Thanksgiving
suggestions.why: Thanksgiving falls on Thursday 26 November 2026. The FoodSafety.gov chart gives the number (poultry 165 °F) and both thermometers on this site are directly relevant.

options.label: A
options.text: Publish a short 'turkey temperature' guide this week, sourced to the official chart, linking both thermometers.
options.tradeoff: Seasonal - traffic, if any, is concentrated in a few days

options.label: B
options.text: Skip seasonal content.
options.tradeoff: Miss a timely, well-sourced topic

suggestions.title: Decide how products are pictured
suggestions.why: Product pages currently use typographic cards and illustrative food photography, never a product photo, because there is no licensed product image source yet. Real product imagery would help buyers.

options.label: A
options.text: Use images through Amazon's sanctioned routes (the official link tools or the Creators API), under the Associates Program IP License.
options.cost: API access or manual image links
options.tradeoff: Must follow the license terms exactly

options.label: B
options.text: Commission original photography of products you own.
options.cost: Buying the products and a shoot
options.tradeoff: Also allows honest hands-on reviews

options.label: C
options.text: Keep illustrative food photography only.
options.tradeoff: Readers never see the product on this site

suggestions.title: Name a real editor
suggestions.why: Guides are signed 'Counter Notes editors' because no person has been named, and an agent must not invent one. A named author with a short bio and an honest description of how products are chosen makes the site read as published.

options.label: A
options.text: You (or a named editor) supply a name, a one-paragraph bio and a photo; it is added to every guide and an About page.
options.tradeoff: Personal visibility

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the editorial-desk byline.
options.tradeoff: Reads as less personal

suggestions.title: Choose the audience's marketplace
suggestions.why: Every link points to amazon.com (United States). Associates programmes are run per country, and the Associates Central country list includes the Netherlands and other EU stores. If readers are mostly outside the US, US links may not convert.

options.label: A
options.text: Stay US-only (amazon.com).
options.tradeoff: Non-US readers land on a store that may not ship to them

options.label: B
options.text: Join a second Associates programme (for example amazon.nl or amazon.de) and show a store choice.
options.tradeoff: More to maintain; each programme has its own rules

suggestions.title: Update the ThermoMaven link to the newer model - or not
suggestions.why: On 2026-11-19 the ThermoMaven listing displayed 'There is a newer model of this item' (B0GL7Z4KP4). Buyers comparing the two may leave through the newer listing.

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the supplied link's destination and add a sentence noting the newer model.
options.tradeoff: Matches what you supplied

options.label: B
options.text: Switch to the newer model after you confirm it in Associates Central.
options.tradeoff: Changes a product you did not supply

suggestions.title: Merge the two thermometer guide sets
suggestions.why: Two sessions published thermometer guides on the same day: the shop guides (shop/guides/) and the thermometer desk (marketing/thermometers/, T64). 'Instant-read or leave-in' is answered on both, so search engines see two pages competing for one question, and readers can land on either.

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the shop guide as the canonical page for each overlapping question, point the other page's canonical tag at it and cross-link the two sets.
options.cost: Edit two generators; agree which page owns each question
options.tradeoff: One page per question; the other remains for readers who arrive there

options.label: B
options.text: Fold the desk's unique guides (accuracy, turkey placement, air-fryer use) into shop/guides/ and retire the duplicates with redirects-by-link.
options.tradeoff: Cleanest structure; most work

options.label: C
options.text: Leave both sets as they are.
options.tradeoff: Duplicate answers compete in search

questions.q: Which exact product did you intend for each of the five short links?
questions.why: Every page promotes the listing each link currently lands on. If any of those is not the product you meant, the content and the link are wrong together.
questions.known: Each code opened one listing on 2026-11-19, the same listing recorded on earlier dates (B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5, B0DZFD6R9Z). The codes are 9 characters, so they are not ASINs themselves.
questions.missing: Your confirmation of the intended ASIN, the official listing URL, the date and how you confirmed it.
questions.how: Reply with the five ASINs, or confirm the five observed ones. They go into the intent fields, kept separate from the observed redirect targets.

questions.q: Is shopnow047c-20 an active tracking ID on an approved amazon.com Associates account?
questions.why: If the account is pending, closed or registered on another marketplace, tagged clicks earn nothing.
questions.known: You supplied the tag on 2026-11-17. It matches the tagged format the link builder enforces. The Operating Agreement and Program Policies govern the account.
questions.missing: Account status, the marketplace it belongs to, and whether a test click registers.
questions.how: Associates Central: check the tracking ID list, click one site link yourself, and look for the click in the report.

questions.q: Are link.amazon short links acceptable Special Links under the current Program Policies?
questions.why: The brief forbids calling them invalid and the question is still open. The site does not use them as product links; it uses dp/ASIN?tag= links instead.
questions.known: The status is recorded as unresolved in Zone3's FLG-003. The Program Policies were updated April 14, 2026.
questions.missing: A statement from Amazon, or a test in your account that shows tracked clicks.
questions.how: Ask Associates support through the Contact Us page in Associates Central, or test one short link while signed in and check the report.

questions.q: Which commission band applies to each product?
questions.why: Commission potential was in the brief, but no rate can be stated per product without the category Amazon assigns.
questions.known: The air fryers sit under Small Appliances and the thermometers under Kitchen Utensils & Gadgets in Amazon's breadcrumbs (observed 2026-11-19). The ledger records why the public rate table does not settle the band (flag F-43).
questions.missing: The authoritative category and band per item.
questions.how: An authenticated Creators API item lookup, or the earnings report after the first qualifying order.

questions.q: Does anybody arrive, and from where?
questions.why: Every content and design decision after this one should be chosen from measured data.
questions.known: No analytics, Search Console or Associates report has been imported. The on-site counter stores counts locally only.
questions.missing: Impressions, queries, landing pages and outbound clicks.
questions.how: Search Console (SG-S03) for search data; the Associates report for clicks and orders; optionally an endpoint (SG-S04).

questions.q: Which buyer questions have real demand?
questions.why: The six guide titles are editorial hypotheses from the brief, not measured topics.
questions.known: None of the titles is backed by search-volume data; the site says so.
questions.how: After four weeks in Search Console, list the queries with impressions and write the next guide for the closest unanswered one.

questions.q: Who is the editor of record?
questions.why: Named authorship makes a site read as published; it cannot be invented.
questions.known: No person has been named in any brief.
questions.missing: A name, a bio and permission to publish them.

questions.q: Which product images may the site use?
questions.why: Product photos help buyers; using them without a licence is a compliance risk.
questions.known: The Program Policies include an IP License section that governs Amazon-provided content. No product image is used on this site today.
questions.missing: A chosen image route and confirmation that it fits the licence.
questions.how: Read the IP License section in the Program Policies; decide SG-S07.

questions.q: Should the ThermoMaven link follow Amazon's 'newer model'?
questions.why: Amazon displays a newer model on the supplied listing.
questions.known: Observed 2026-11-19: 'There is a newer model of this item' pointing at B0GL7Z4KP4 (orange).
questions.missing: Your preference, and a verified spec read of the newer listing if you switch.

questions.q: Which country are your readers in?
questions.why: Links go to amazon.com; a reader in the EU may need a different store.
questions.known: All links target amazon.com. The Associates Central country list includes the United States, the Netherlands, Germany and other stores.
questions.how: Search Console country report once verified (SG-S03).

questions.q: Which of the conflicting manufacturer and Amazon figures is right?
questions.why: Three spec conflicts are published as conflicts: the 8 Qt Chefman's maximum temperature, and the Emeril's preset and accessory counts.
questions.known: Both readings of each are on official pages read 2026-11-19.
questions.how: Check the printed manual (Emeril's store links its product manual PDF) or ask each manufacturer's support; then record the answer with that source.

design_prompt.intro: Inputs to paste into the next design prompt. They describe the site as it should feel to a buyer; none of them changes a verified value.
items: A small, honest kitchen-gear publication: 'Counter Notes - kitchen gear, explained before you buy.' Products first, method second, audit trail out of sight but one click away.
Plain, specific, second person. Short sentences. Say what a spec means for dinner. Never 'game-changer', 'elevate', 'ultimate', 'must-have'. Never claim to have tested something nobody tested.
1) one-line promise and hero image, 2) the five products as cards with a 'best for' label, 3) category tiles, 4) newest guides, 5) 'how we pick' in three lines, 6) footer with every dashboard.
Verdict in one sentence, good fit / think twice, the price button, the sourced spec table, related guides, then the link-intent record at the bottom.

Warm paper background, near-black ink, one terracotta accent, a serif display face for headlines, a clean sans for body, generous whitespace, 8-px spacing grid, cards with hairline borders not heavy shadows.
Food and kitchens only until licensed product images exist; every illustrative image labelled as such.

Disclosure strip directly under the masthead on every page and repeated in the footer; '(paid link)' next to every price button; rel="sponsored nofollow" on every product link; no price, rating or review count printed.
Home, Air fryers, Meat thermometers, Guides, Compare - plus one 'Behind the scenes' menu that holds the briefing, flags and every dashboard.
